comment: Expected failures caused by the Python SDK (python-sdk, paths relative to src/acp/) or the Python interop programs. Owned by programs/python. See README.md in this directory.

expectations.reason: The SDK's HTTP server never enables the unstable router: session/fork is answered method-not-found
The SDK's WebSocket server never enables the unstable router: session/fork is answered method-not-found

The Python interop client does not send $/cancel_request: python-sdk sends one only when the task awaiting a pending request is cancelled (connection.py:230), which drops the response the step checks, and has no call to send one for a given id

The Python interop client does not send $/cancel_request: python-sdk has no call to send one for an arbitrary (here unknown) request id, only the implicit send on a cancelled pending request (connection.py:230)

The Python interop agent does not send $/cancel_request (python-sdk sends one only when the task awaiting a pending request is cancelled, connection.py:230; the program does not use it yet), so it answers the chunk "cancel-request unsupported" instead of "cancel-request sent"

The Python interop agent does not send $/cancel_request for its pending fs/read_text_file (python-sdk sends one only from a cancelled pending request, connection.py:230; the program does not use it yet)
create_websocket_stream connects with websockets' default max_size of 1 MiB and offers no way to raise it; a 1 MiB chunk plus its envelope exceeds it and the client closes the socket with 1009
create_websocket_stream connects with websockets' default max_size of 1 MiB and offers no way to raise it; the client closes the socket with 1009

ToolCall's kind and status are closed Literals whose wrap validator (use_default_on_error) replaces an unknown value with None: the tool call surfaces with the raw status interop_future_status (and kind) dropped, so the value is lost rather than kept open

PlanEntry.priority and status are closed Literals (schema.py:3542, :3547) and Plan.entries skips invalid items: the entry with interop_future_priority/interop_future_status is silently dropped and the plan surfaces empty
PromptResponse.stopReason is a closed Literal with no lenient validator: a response with stopReason interop_future_stop fails the prompt call with a pydantic ValidationError (the connection survives)

Annotations.audience is List[Literal["assistant", "user"]] with skip_invalid_items: the agent receives the prompt but the unknown Role interop_future_role is silently dropped, so it reads [user] and chunks "audience: user"
Annotations.audience skips invalid items: the Python agent's handler sees audience ['user'], interop_future_role dropped before it
